items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: when we would do a concert that had something to do with Rugolo, I would be in his garage for two or three days finding all these original scores... enabled us to be able to do the events and present all these things

ctx.x: Yeah. And how do you take the pulse of the Southern California area to try to program the acts and the artists that will bring those people? Is it partly your radio work or word of mouth?

It depends what it is and what we’re doing because kind of the sequence of events for me was what used to be KLON Radio in Long Beach, which now is K-JAZZ, so I was there for 13 or 14 years producing concerts and festivals and on the air as well. Then the Los Angeles Jazz Institute, which I still operate the Jazz Institute, but then almost ten years ago now I became the general manager at KSDS in San Diego because I truly wanted to see jazz radio continue. And I decided I could continue to do all the other things…

again, you know there’s — our job with radio is to promote what the local promoters are doing, to try to help them, not to compete against them. So we do things — again — for a purpose. Sometimes the purpose is as a fundraiser for the radio station. Sometimes it’s to showcase something or an artist or maybe to celebrate a historical occasion or to celebrate something — a new release, or whatever the case may be. Jazz Institute is a little bit different in that the archive is the centerpiece of the Jazz Institute.…
